NEW DELHI: The international legal architecture must be more democratic, inclusive and sensitive to the realities of the Global South, external affairs minister S Jaishankar said Friday. At the 60th anniversary of UNCITRAL, he said: "Today's world is witnessing unprecedented geopolitical volatility, supply chain disruptions, rapid technological shifts. Article Title: 'Thank you, friends': PM Modi hails 'love, support' of youth in new Insta video
Article Text:
Thank you, friends': PM Modi hails 'love, support' of youth in new Insta video

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday thanked young people for watching his video on examination reforms and sharing their suggestions.In a video message shared on Instagram, PM Modi expressed appreciation for the response to his address and the feedback received from students and young people."Thank you friends. I had the opportunity to meet you late last night. I appreciate the way you responded to my video and your positive suggestions. Thanks to everyone..." PM Modi said."Last night, I got the opportunity to interact with you. The way you responded to the video I posted and shared your positive suggestions—thanks to everybody. Your love and support continue, and that our connection grows even stronger and more active," he further said.The caption of the video read: "Thanks to the youngsters who watched my video yesterday and sent insightful suggestions."PM Modi's message comes a day after he announced that the government would introduce stricter measures to tackle examination paper leaks amid nationwide protests over alleged irregularities in the NEET-UG examination.In a video message on Thursday, PM Modi said the Union Cabinet would consider a draft Bill providing for fast-track courts and stringent punishment for those involved in paper leak cases, with efforts to pass the legislation in Parliament during the coming week."I know that paper leak is not an ordinary issue. It is very painful for lakhs of students and their guardians," the Prime Minister had said, adding that the government had already arrested those responsible and ensured that nearly 22 lakh students were able to retake the examination without losing an academic year.He had also said the proposed legislation would include provisions for fast-track courts and tougher penalties to strengthen the integrity of the country's examination system.The announcement came amid widespread protests over the alleged NEET-UG paper leak. Earlier this week, PM Modi also told the NDA Parliamentary Party that the government was working to make the country's examination system "foolproof".
Article Summary: Prime minister narendra modi thanks young people for watching his video on examination reforms. In a video message shared on instagram, pm modi expressed appreciation for the response to his address. Pm modi's message comes a day after he announced that the government would introduce stricter measures to tackle examination paper leaks.

Article Title: Grain, not guns: MEA rejects Russia's claim on deadly ship attack that killed 4 Indians
Article Text:
India reiterates concerns to Russia

Shipping attacks under scrutiny

NEW DELHI: Ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Friday said the merchant vessel MV Golden Leo, which was struck in a Russian attack off Ukraine's Odesa port earlier this week, was carrying grain and not military cargo, effectively rejecting Moscow's assertion that the ship was transporting weapons for Ukraine.Responding to questions on the Russian claim, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said the information available with the Indian government showed the Guinea-Bissau-flagged vessel had loaded grain before leaving Odesa."As per information made available to us from the Directorate General of Maritime Administration, India, MV Golden Leo, the Guinea-Bissau-flagged commercial vessel involved in the tragic incident in the Odesa port, had loaded grain as cargo prior to its departure on July 19," Jaiswal said at the ministry's weekly media briefing."We once again reiterate that commercial shipping and seafarers must not be targeted under any circumstances," he added.The clarification came days after a Russian strike on the merchant vessel killed 10 people, including four Indian seafarers, marking the first deaths of Indian sailors since the Russia-Ukraine war began.Jaiswal said external affairs minister S Jaishankar reiterated India's position during his meeting with Russian foreign minister Sergey Lavrov in Manila on Wednesday.India had also summoned Russian Charge d'Affaires Vladimir Ladanov on Tuesday to convey its "grave concerns" and "unequivocal condemnation" of the attack on the commercial vessel.The move followed remarks by Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov, who defended Russia's actions, saying Moscow would continue targeting vessels carrying arms for Ukraine.Peskov said Russian forces would continue striking ships involved in transporting "ammunition, weapons, and so on" for the Kyiv government.India's latest statement, citing cargo details provided by the directorate general of maritime administration, contradicts that assertion.MV Golden Leo, carrying 17 crew members including five Indians, was hit by Russian cruise missiles while leaving the Ukrainian port of Odesa.The attack has intensified India's concerns over the safety of commercial shipping in the conflict zone.Separately, the MEA also condemned another attack on the commercial vessel MV OMORFI in the Black Sea that killed an Indian national, calling attacks on commercial shipping "unacceptable" and urging all parties to ensure the safety of maritime navigation and the uninterrupted flow of global trade.With two fatal incidents involving Indian seafarers in less than a week, India has repeatedly stressed that civilian merchant vessels and their crews must not be targeted during the ongoing conflict.
Article Summary: Mv golden leo, carrying 17 crew members including five indians, was hit by russian cruise missiles while leaving the ukrainian port of odesa. The move followed remarks by kremlin spokesperson dmitry peskov, who defended russia's actions, saying moscow would continue targeting vessels carrying arms for ukraine.

Article Title: Govt dismisses Pak allegation of India deliberately causing flooding
Article Text:
1

2

Govt dismissed Pakistan's allegation that India is deliberately causing flooding as baseless, saying the recent increase in flows in Chenab river is a direct consequence of intense monsoon rainfall over Jammu and adjoining catchment areas from July 20 to 23.Govt also reiterated India's position on the Indus Waters Treaty that it will continue to be held in abeyance until Pakistan credibly and irrevocably abjures its support for cross-border terrorism. However, it also said India will continue to share high flood data with Pakistan on humanitarian grounds.MEA said Pakistan's flood forecasting division, in its July 22 flood advisory, had attributed high flood levels in Chenab to heavy rainfall over the upper catchment and stated high flows at Marala were expected to persist before gradually receding as rainfall over the catchment decreased."The rise in river flows is a natural hydrological response to heavy monsoon rainfall and not the result of any deliberate action by India. Attempts to portray a weather-driven flood event as an upstream intervention are factually incorrect, technically untenable, and contradicted by Pakistan's own official flood advisories," said MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal.On allegations related to flood warnings, he said river flows during this period did not reach extraordinary discharge levels requiring issuance of flood warnings. According to India, observed flows were consistent with prevailing monsoon conditions over the upper catchments, as acknowledged by Pakistan's flood forecasting authorities." ...like last year, India will share high flood data with Pakistan on humanitarian grounds, through diplomatic channels as and when a situation arises," he said.
Article Summary: Govt says recent increase in flows in chenab river is a direct consequence of intense monsoon rainfall over jammu and adjoining catchment areas from july 20 to 23. India will continue to share high flood data with pakistan on humanitarian grounds.

Article Title: Government objects to China illegally occupying Indian territory
Article Text:
‘Delhi Consistent In Not Violating Beijing Sovereignty’ ‘Delhi Consistent In Not Violating Beijing Sovereignty’ ‘Delhi Consistent In Not Violating Beijing Sovereignty’ ‘Delhi Consistent In Not Violating Beijing Sovereignty’ ‘Delhi Consistent In Not Violating Beijing Sovereignty’ 1

2

NEW DELHI: India has been consistent in not violating China's sovereignty, but China continues to illegally occupy Indian territory in J&K and Ladakh, said govt, days after external affairs minister S Jaishankar's meeting with his counterpart Wang Yi.The assertion was in response to a question at a media briefing on the Chinese readout of the meeting in which it quoted Jaishankar as saying India's positions on issues concerning Taiwan and Tibet have not changed, and India respects China's sovereignty."EAM said (to Wang) when it comes to sovereignty issues, it is India that should be and is raising them. India does not violate China's sovereignty in any manner and has been consistent," said MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal."But China has been in illegal occupation of Indian territory in J&K and Ladakh since 1963, where India's right is officially acknowledged even by China. Also, there are Chinese projects on territories in J&K that belong to India, we object to that," he added, alluding to Chinese projects in POK.The meeting between Jaishankar and Wang Yi in Manila on the margins of Asean saw Jaishankar stressing the need to address issues like bilateral trade imbalance, need for fair market access and reliability of supply chains.He also underlined that border peace and tranquillity will remain a prerequisite for normalisation of bilateral ties.While the Indian readout didn't mention Tibet or Taiwan issue, a Chinese statement later said Jaishankar had backed China's sovereignty. India follows the one-China policy like most other countries but without publicly articulating it since 2010.Wang said in the meeting China will continue to support India in hosting a successful Brics summit this year. The summit, which India will host in Sept, is likely to be attended by President Xi Jinping. This will be Xi's first visit to India since 2019, when he travelled to Mahabalipuram for the second India-China summit.
Article Summary: China continues to illegally occupy indian territory in j&k and ladakh, says govt. This comes after external affairs minister s jaishankar's meeting with his counterpart wang yi. China will continue to support india in hosting a successful brics summit this year.

Article Title: The only judges that matter
Article Text: Thirukkural with the Times explores real-world lessons from the classic Tamil text ‘Thirukkural’. Written by Tamil poet and philosopher Thiruvalluvar, the Kural consists of 1,330 short couplets of seven words each. This text is divided into three books with teachings on virtue, wealth, and love and is considered one of the great works ever on ethics and morality. The Kural has influenced scholars and leaders across social, political, and philosophical spheres. Motivational speaker, author and diversity champion Bharathi Bhaskar explores the masterpiece. Every time the winners of a major award are announced, celebrations begin in one corner, controversies in another. The latter often outlives the former. History, however, offers a strange consolation. Awards do not always decide greatness. Time often does. Take Mahakavi Bharathiyar. His immortal poem ‘Senthamizh naadenum pothinile, inba thene vandhu paayudhu kaadhinile’ flows through the veins of every Tamilian today. Yet, when Bharathiyar's friends submitted this poem for a poetry competition, it won only the second prize . Does anyone remember the poem which won the first prize? The irony repeats itself elsewhere. Mahatma Gandhi was nominated several times for the Nobel Peace Prize but never received it. If the apostle of Ahimsa did not fit the definition of a peace laureate, who possibly could? Alfred Hitchcock never won an Oscar despite creating masterpieces like Psycho, Vertigo and Rear Window , films that continue to define the language of cinema. Leo Tolstoy, Virginia Woolf and James Joyce never received the Nobel Prize. Perhaps the most heartbreaking omission was that of Rosalind Franklin. Her pioneering X-ray crystallography images were indispensable to deciphering the structure of DNA. Yet the Nobel Prize in medicine recognised only Watson, Crick and Wilkins. Many readers would remember Jeyamohan's unforgettable short story Yaanai Doctor . Doctor K—modelled on the legendary elephant veterinarian V Krishnamurthy—is recommended for the Padma Shri. Political currents intervene and the honour slips away. That very night, however, a herd of elephants arrives at his doorstep with an injured calf. They have travelled nearly 100km, instinctively searching for the one human they trust. Doctor K quietly treats the animal. What greater recognition can there be than the trust of beings that cannot speak? Some honours are conferred by institutions. Others are bestowed by life itself. These thoughts returned to me while reading the list of the 72nd National Film Awards. Cinema is deeply subjective and different juries value different attributes. Yet many film lovers, myself included, were left perplexed. In my own reckoning, Meiyazhagan deserved to stand among the year's finest films. The film made kindness, innocence and warmth compelling without ever becoming sentimental. Karthi's effortless body language and emotional sincerity became the soul of the film. Maharaja too was a masterclass in layered storytelling. Vijay Sethupathi delivered one of the most restrained performances of his career. Thiruvalluvar expressed a similar sentiment nearly 2,000 years ago, in Kural 849. "Kaanadhaan kaattuvaan; thaan kaanaan. Kaanaadhaan kandaanaam thaan kanda vaaru." “One who presents the unseen as seen will not come forward to see what is to be seen.” Perhaps that is also a gentle reminder of the limits of human judgment. Perhaps another jury , on another day, would have arrived at different conclusions. Awards are human judgments, not eternal truths. Fortunately, artists have always understood something juries forget. Their true audience is not the few who sit around a table but the countless unknown hearts across generations. Rudyard Kipling captured this wisdom in the poem If— : "If you can meet with Triumph and Disaster And treat those two impostors just the same..." Awards and snubs are both impostors. Neither defines an artist. One inflates, the other disappoints; both are temporary. Time is the only jury that never retires. Its verdict may be slow, but it is seldom wrong.
Article Summary: Thirukkural with the times explores real-world lessons from the classic tamil text. Written by tamil poet and philosopher thiruvalluvar, the kural consists of 1,330 short couplets of seven words each. This text is divided into three books with teachings on virtue, wealth, and love.

Article Title: Amid manhunt for J&K cop’s terrorist killers, detentions spike to 3.5k
Article Text:
Detentions across J&K linked to the terrorist killing of head constable Ashiq Hussain Qureshi rose to 3,500

SRINAGAR: Detentions across J&K linked to the terrorist killing of head constable Ashiq Hussain Qureshi rose to 3,500 Friday as police stepped up their crackdown on suspected sympathisers of armed groups.A senior police officer said around 700 people were detained for interrogation in Srinagar alone since the terror attack last Wednesday, in which Qureshi, who was on Amarnath Yatra duty at Lal Chowk in Anantnag, was killed. “Due process has been followed in all detentions,” he said.DGP Nalin Prabhat convened a meeting for a comprehensive security review in Srinagar, with participating officers presenting their assessments of the prevailing security scenario across the Union territory.“The meeting focused on the current operational environment, threat perception and preparedness of field formations,” a police spokesperson said. “The DGP directed the officers to intensify area domination and night domination, particularly in vulnerable urban areas.”Home minister Amit Shah had a phone conversation with the slain head constable’s son after J&K leader of the opposition Sunil Sharma visited the family at their residence in Lalpora Beerwah of Budgam.Lieutenant governor Manoj Sinha, too, made a trip earlier and assured the bereaved family of the administration’s support.CM Omar Abdullah was critical of the detentions and Thursday’s controlled explosions targeting the family homes of two wanted Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorists. “I understand the police’s anger. But there is a Supreme Court order that such summary action should not be taken,” he said.Recalling his first stint as CM when J&K was a state, Omar said he knew “at the time that this problem (terrorism) cannot be resolved without the people’s support”.He said the backlash against terrorist outfits after last year’s attack on tourists in Pahalgam showed that ordinary people do not support them. “Even today, people are angry that a police head constable has been killed so brutally. But when the number of arrests rises from hundreds to 2,000 or 2,500, that public anger risks being redirected against us,” he said. “I hope we take our people along with us in this fight.”Ex-CM and PDP chief Mehbooba Mufti said detaining thousands and demolishing the family homes of two “alleged” terrorists “amounts to collective punishment that has no place in a democracy”. People’s Conference chairperson Sajad Lone warned that the police’s response to one of their own being killed by terrorists would “do more harm”.
Article Summary: Detentions across j&k linked to the terrorist killing of head constable ashiq hussain qureshi rose to 3,500 friday. Police stepped up their crackdown on suspected sympathisers of armed groups. A senior police officer said around 700 people were detained for interrogation in srinagar alone since the terror attack last wednesday.

Article Title: Indian seafarer killed after ship attacked in Black Sea; MEA condemns incident
Article Text:
Indian seafarer killed after ship attacked in Black Sea; MEA condemns incident

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs on Friday condemned the attack on the commercial vessel MV OMORFI in the Black Sea that killed an Indian national, calling attacks on commercial shipping 'unacceptable' and urging all parties to ensure the safety of maritime navigation and global trade.The incident took place on July 18, when the MV OMORFI was attacked while transiting the Black Sea, reportedly in Russian territorial waters. According to the MEA, there were 10 crew members on board, including three Indian nationals. One Indian citizen was killed in the attack, while the other two Indians are reported to be safe.In a statement, the MEA said, "On 18 July 2026, the commercial vessel MV OMORFI was attacked while transiting the Black Sea, reportedly in Russian territorial waters. At the time of the incident, there were ten crew members on board, including three Indian nationals. As per available information, one Indian national tragically lost his life in the attack. We extend our deepest condolences to the bereaved family of the deceased. The other two Indian nationals on board are reported to be safe."Condemning the attack, the ministry said, "India unequivocally condemns such attacks targeting commercial shipping and placing the lives of innocent civilian crew members at risk.It is a matter of serious concern that the freedom of navigation and international commerce is facing increasing threats. India calls upon all concerned parties to uphold international obligations to ensure the safety and security of maritime navigation and uninterrupted flow of global commerce. "The latest attack comes after MV Golden Leo, a Guinea-Bissau-flagged cargo vessel, was struck shortly after departing Ukraine's port of Odesa on July 19. The vessel had 17 crew members, including five Indian nationals. Four Indians were killed and one was critically injured in that attack.The MEA had then condemned the strike, saying commercial shipping and civilian crew members should not be targeted, while assuring that India's mission in Ukraine was extending all possible assistance to those affected.The back-to-back attacks have heightened concerns over the safety of commercial shipping in the Black Sea, where renewed hostilities have increased risks to civilian vessels and global maritime trade.
Article Summary: Indian seafarer killed after ship attacked in black sea; mea condemns incident. One indian citizen was killed in the attack, while the other two indians are reported to be safe. Back-to-back attacks have heightened concerns over the safety of commercial shipping in the black sea.

Article Title: PM Modi gains 1 million Instagram followers overnight after selfie video amid NEET protest
Article Text:
PM Modi gains 1 million Instagram followers overnight after selfie video

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi gained around 1 million Instagram followers overnight after he released his selfie video on Thursday night addressing concerns of the NEET paper leak.Currently PM Modi has 102 million followers on Instagram. His video captioned: "More strict actions against paper leaks to come in tomorrow’s Cabinet!" has garnered 271 million views so far along with 15 million likes and 1.3 million comments on Instagram.In the video, he announced that the government would introduce tougher measures to tackle examination paper leaks. He also informed about the Union Cabinet meeting agenda held on Friday."I know that paper leak is not an ordinary issue. It is very painful for lakh of students and their guardians," he said."Numerous effective measures have been taken in the past two and a half months since the paper leak incident. The culprits have been caught and are in jail. Our most important responsibility was to ensure that students' year is not wasted. The government used all its might to ensure that 22 lakh students could take their exams in the shortest possible time," he added.The Union Cabinet on Friday cleared amendments to the anti-paper leak law, proposing stricter punishment for those involved in examination paper leaks. Sources said the revised law prescribes up to 10 years in prison and a fine of as much as Rs 10 crore, while raising the minimum jail term from three years to five years.
Article Summary: Pm modi gains 1 million instagram followers overnight after selfie video. His video captioned: "more strict actions against paper leaks to come in tomorrow’s cabinet!" Has garnered 271 million views so far along with 15 million likes and 1.3 million comments on instagram.

Article Title: 'Position remains unchanged': India rejects Pakistan's Asean remarks, reiterates stand on Indus Waters Treaty
Article Text:
'Position remains unchanged': India rejects Pakistan's Asean remarks, reiterates stand on Indus Waters Treaty

NEW DELHI: External affairs ministry on Friday strongly rejected Pakistan's remarks at the Asean Regional Forum and reiterated that India's position on the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) remains unchanged, saying the treaty will remain in abeyance until Pakistan 'irrevocably and credibly' ends its support for cross-border terrorism.The MEA also dismissed Pakistan's allegations that India had deliberately caused flooding in Pakistan, calling the claims 'baseless' and attributing the rise in the Chenab river's water level to heavy monsoon rainfall.Addressing a weekly media briefing, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said Pakistan had used the Asean forum to raise issues that India had already rejected."On the ASEAN forum, Pakistan utilised it to make certain remarks. On that, we have made categorical rejections of the issues raised through our press release. You would have seen our statement. On the Indus Waters Treaty, our position remains unchanged and very clear. The Indus Waters Treaty remains in abeyance until Pakistan irrevocably and credibly abjures its support for cross-border terrorism," Jaiswal said.The remarks came a day after India categorically rejected Pakistan's comments at the Asean Regional Forum in Manila, accusing Islamabad of using the multilateral platform to spread 'state-sponsored disinformation' and divert attention from its record of sponsoring cross-border terrorism.Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister and foreign minister Ishaq Dar, who represented Islamabad at the forum, raised the Jammu and Kashmir issue and criticised India's decision to keep the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance.India responded by stating that Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh 'have been, are and will always remain integral and inalienable parts of India' and that Pakistan had no locus standi to comment on the matter.Responding to another question during the briefing, Jaiswal rejected Pakistani media reports alleging that India had deliberately caused flooding in Pakistan by manipulating river flows."We have seen Pakistani media reports alleging that India is deliberately causing flooding in Pakistan and such allegations are baseless and contrary to the facts," he said.Jaiswal said the recent increase in the Chenab river's flow was caused by intense monsoon rainfall over Jammu and adjoining catchment areas between July 20 and 23.He observed that Pakistan's own Flood Forecasting Division in Lahore had, in its advisory issued on July 22, attributed the high flood levels in the Chenab to heavy rainfall over the upper catchment and had forecast that the high flows would gradually recede as rainfall decreased."The rise in river flows is, therefore, a natural hydrological response to heavy monsoon rainfall and not the result of any deliberate action by India. Attempts to portray a weather-driven flood event as an upstream intervention are factually incorrect, technically untenable, and contradicted by Pakistan's own official flood advisories," Jaiswal said.He also rejected allegations that India had failed to issue flood warnings, saying river flows during the period did not reach levels requiring special alerts."Any suggestion that India deliberately withheld flood-related information is, therefore, without factual basis. Nevertheless, like last year, India will share high-flood data with Pakistan on humanitarian grounds, through diplomatic channels as and when a situation arises," he added.External affairs minister S Jaishankar attended the Asean-India, East Asia Summit and Asean Regional Forum ministerial meetings in Manila over the last two days.
Article Summary: 'position remains unchanged': india rejects pakistan's asean remarks, reiterates stand on indus waters treaty. Mea also dismissed pakistan's allegations that india had deliberately caused flooding in pakistan, calling the claims 'baseless' and attributing the rise in the chenab river's water level to heavy monsoon rainfall.

Article Title: 'There are Chinese projects on territories in J&K that belong to India': MEA objects to illegal occupation
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Ministry of external affairs on Friday accused China of violating India's sovereignty and said that it is "illegally occupying" Indian territories in Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh.During a weekly press briefing, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that the government objects to the Chinese projects in Jammu and Kashmir."EAM said that when it comes to sovereignty issues, it is actually India that should be and is raising them. India does not violate China’s sovereignty in any manner and has been consistent," Jaiswal said."But China has been in illegal occupation of Indian territories in Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh since 1963, where India’s right is officially acknowledged even by China. There are Chinese projects on territories in Jammu and Kashmir that belong to India, and we object to that," he added.This comes a day after external affairs minister S Jaishankar met his Chinese counterpart Wang Yi on the sidelines of Asean summit in Manila,According to the Chinese foreign ministry readout, Wang said the meetings between Chinese President Xi Jinping and Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Kazan and Tianjin had "guided China-India relations onto the right track of improvement and development.""China and India are partners, not competitors, and opportunities, not threats, for each other," Wang said, adding that institutional exchanges between the two countries had gradually resumed, border areas had maintained peace and tranquillity, and bilateral trade had reached a new high."These achievements have not come easily and should be cherished," he said.Calling China and India representatives of emerging economies and key members of the Global South, Wang said the two countries should "prioritise human well-being, demonstrate their responsibility as major powers, consolidate the positive momentum of bilateral relations, strengthen coordination and cooperation in international and regional affairs, and make positive contributions to promoting multipolarity and the democratisation of international relations. "He said China was willing to work with India to implement the consensus reached by the two leaders, maintain close high-level exchanges, expand cooperation in trade, media and people-to-people exchanges, properly handle sensitive issues, and "explore a correct way for neighbouring major powers to coexist peacefully, based on mutual respect, mutual trust, common development, and common prosperity.
Article Summary: Mea spokesperson randhir jaiswal said that the government objects to the chinese projects in jammu and kashmir. This comes a day after external affairs minister s jaishankar met his chinese counterpart wang yi. Wang said the meetings between chinese president xi jinping and prime minister narendra modi had "guided china-india relations onto the right track of improvement and development"

Article Title: 'Don't insult students' intelligence': Rahul Gandhi slams PM Modi's midnight video on paper leaks
Article Text:
Poll Vote & Share your view What should be the government's priority in response to the NEET-UG paper leak? Ensuring accountability Strengthening exam security 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi early Friday attacked Prime Minister Narendra Modi accusing him of sidestepping the demand for Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan 's resignation over the alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leak.Reacting to the Prime Minister's late-night video message on the issue, Rahul said PM Modi should not "insult the intelligence" of students and demanded Pradhan be sacked saying the PM's address failed to raise students' key concerns.In a post on X, Rahul wrote, "Mr Modi, our students are demanding Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation. Don't insult their intelligence with this pathetic midnight video."Listing his demands, he said:"1. Sack Pradhan.2. Punish those who beat students.3. Apologise."The leader of oppostion's remarks came hours after Prime Minister Modi announced that the government would bring a Bill in Parliament next week providing for stringent punishment against those involved in examination paper leaks.In a self-recorded video shared on X late Thursday night, the Prime Minister said the proposed legislation, which includes provisions for Fast-Track Courts and stricter penalties, would be discussed by the Union Cabinet on Friday before being introduced in Parliament when the second week of the Monsoon Session begins on Monday."Friends, I know that paper leaks are not an ordinary matter. For lakhs of students and their parents, it is extremely painful," PM Modi said."Our most important responsibility was to ensure that a whole year for the students is not wasted. It was very important to conduct the exams immediately. The government used its full strength to arrange exams for nearly 22 lakh students in the shortest possible time. And just five or six days ago, on the 19th, the results were also announced," he said.The Prime Minister said the government was now moving towards stronger legal action."Today I have issued directions to the departments to set up Fast-Track Courts. The departments worked tirelessly and, late last night, provided me with a draft. This draft, which includes provisions for Fast-Track Courts and stringent punishments, will be discussed in the Cabinet tomorrow," he said.He added that after incorporating suggestions from Cabinet colleagues, the Bill would be finalised and introduced in Parliament next week."Nothing is more important than the welfare and future of our youth. Those who try to harm the future of our youth will not be spared," PM Modi said.The opposition has been demanding Pradhan's resignation and a detailed discussion on the alleged NEET-UG paper leak during the Monsoon Session, with the issue triggering protests both inside Parliament and on the streets.Activist Sonam Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike on Friday at Medanta Hospital in the presence of Union ministers J P Nadda and Jitendra Singh, along with senior leaders of the Apex Body of Leh.In a post on X, Wangchuk said he decided to end the fast after prolonged discussions and in view of the possibility of violence."Just now in the presence of Union Ministers JP Nadda & Dr. Jitendra Singh and the senior leaders of Apex Body of Leh Ladakh I finally broke my fast after 26 days... This was done after a long negotiation on various conditions and in view of possible violence in the country," he said."I will explain the conditions in detail in a separate video very soon. Meanwhile urge you all to stay very vigilant about not allowing violence of any kind anywhere," he added.Meanwhile, the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) has called for nationwide peaceful protests on Friday, reiterating its demand for Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation over the alleged examination irregularities.
Article Summary: Rahul gandhi accuses prime minister narendra modi of sidestepping the demand for union education minister dharmendra pradhan's resignation over the alleged neet-ug 2026 paper leak. NEW DELHI: India slammed Pakistan for raising issues related to J&K and the Indus Waters Treaty at the Asean Regional Forum, saying the remarks by Pakistani foreign minister Ishaq Dar were baseless and unwarranted.The govt said in a statement it was no surprise that a multilateral forum had once again been cynically exploited by Pakistan to amplify falsehoods, peddle state-sponsored disinformation, and divert attention from its own well-documented record of sponsoring cross-border terrorism.External affairs minister S Jaishankar had said at the same forum that acts of terrorism will have consequences. NEW DELHI: Activist Sonam Wangchuk on Friday ended his 26-day indefinite hunger strike after receiving assurances from the Centre that key demands raised by students protesting over alleged examination irregularities would be addressed.In a post on X, Wangchuk said the government had assured that there would be a discussion in Parliament on accountability in the examination system, compensation for families of students who died by suicide following the recent NEET paper leak, and no cases against peaceful protesters."END OF HUNGER... BEGINNING OF ACCOUNTABILITY...!" Wangchuk wrote.He added, "Sonam Wangchuk ends his fast after 26 days upon getting assurance from the government and members of parliament of all political parties that the issue of accountability in the failing examination system will be discussed on the floors of the Indian Parliament.""The government also gave assurance that families of suicide victims in the recent NEET examination paper leak will be given adequate compensation and that there will be no cases registered against the peacefully protesting students and youths," he said.Wangchuk announced the end of his fast after Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh met him at Medanta Hospital in Gurugram around midnight and conveyed the government's assurances."Just now in the presence of Union Ministers JP Nadda, Dr Jitendra Singh and the senior leaders of Apex Body of Leh Ladakh, I finally broke my fast after 26 days," Wangchuk wrote.He said 65 Members of Parliament from different political parties had either visited him or signed letters urging him to end the fast."This was done after long negotiations on various conditions and in view of possible violence in the country. Meanwhile, I urge you all to stay very vigilant about not allowing violence of any kind anywhere," he said.Prime Minister Narendra Modi welcomed Wangchuk's decision to end the fast. Article Title: WWE Hall of Famer Jim Ross backs Vince McMahon's interest in returning to wrestling amid his lawsuit saga
Article Text:
Vince McMahon-Janel Grant lawsuit heading to private arbitration in latest update (Image via: Netflix)

Jim Ross agrees Vince McMahon could return to wrestling but rules out the possibility of joining AEW



Grilling JR

(source: WrestleZone)

As speculation is doing the rounds that there is a possibility that Vince McMahon is planning to return to WWE , Hall of Famer Jim Ross has recently backed McMahon's interest in wrestling and believes that he is far from finished with professional wrestling.The rumor gained attention after his lawsuit with former employee Janel Grant was moved from federal court to confidential arbitration. This prompted rumors about whether the former chairman would return to the company now.It is to be noted that McMahon had retired from WWE in July 2022 after the hush money scandal arose. He later returned as an executive chairman in 2023, but his stint was short, as following Janel Grant’s lawsuit, he had to resign from the company in January 2024.Amid the ongoing speculation, WWE Hall of Famer Jim Ross believes that Vince McMahon is not yet done with wrestling and might return by buying TNA for a comeback. However, the legendary commentator dismissed the idea of McMahon working alongside AEW president Tony Khan.Earlier, the discussion actually gained momentum after Dave Meltzer claimed that it would not shock him if he were brought back in this position. Though he didn't say it with utter conviction, he said it wouldn't shock him if he decided to return.He was not stating it as an expectation but rather as a possibility.He also suggested that if McMahon ever returns to WWE, it wouldn't be a meaningful position, because he would not replace President Nick Khan or shift Chief Content Officer Paul "Triple H" Levesque, his son-in-law.Meanwhile, after Jim Ross was asked about the possibility of the former WWE chairman returning to wrestling, he said he would likely do it his own way.Speaking on the latest episode of hispodcast, Ross suggested that McMahon might return to the wrestling scenario. However, he predicted that McMahon would be more likely to acquire another promotion, such as TNA Wrestling, if he chooses to get back into the industry.Even during the podcast, host Conrad Thompson asked whether McMahon could ever work with Tony Khan in AEW. Ross dismissed the idea, as he believes that Tony Khan probably wouldn’t be interested in bringing McMahon into AEW.“Unlikely. Unlikely. He’s going to want to steer his own ship, build his own boat and take it from there. Off top of my head, I’d say probably not. And I don’t see Tony Khan wanting to do business with him either,” he stated.Vince McMahon has spent decades running WWE in a higher position until he had to resign due to his legal issues. So, it would be difficult for him to take a smaller role in another company, Ross has further suggested.He also believes that it’s difficult to keep McMahon away from the wrestling scene. He further added, “He’s going to be doing something that allows him to display his product knowledge. And God almighty, he’s got plenty of product knowledge. He should be fine.”Meanwhile, the federal lawsuit filed by former WWE employee Janel Grant against chairman Vince McMahon and WWE has now moved out of the public court system, and both parties have agreed to file for confidential arbitration. Following this decision, the lawsuit will be dismissed shortly from the federal court.
Article Summary: Vince mcmahon-janel grant lawsuit heading to private arbitration in latest update. Jim ross agrees vince mcmahon could return to wrestling but rules out the possibility of joining aew. The federal lawsuit filed by former wwe employee janel grant against chairman vince mcmahon and wwe has now moved out of the public court system.

Article Title: 'Getting IV drips every morning': CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke diagnosed with typhoid
Article Text:
CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke





NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Saturday said he has been diagnosed with typhoid but asserted that the agitation will continue until Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigns.In a video message, Dipke thanked CJP supporters, whom he referred to as "cockroaches", for carrying out peaceful protests across the country and credited them for the success of the movement."Hello everyone. As you all know, I was not feeling well for the last few days. So, blood reports have come. And I have been diagnosed with typhoid. And my treatment is going on. I am getting IV drips every morning and evening.""But I really want to thank all the cockroaches who are peacefully protesting all over the country. And you have made this movement so successful. A big big thank you to all. And congratulations to you all for making this movement such a big big success," he added.Despite his illness, Dipke expressed confidence that the protests would achieve their objective, saying the movement would continue until Pradhan steps down.The remarks came as CJP reiterated that it may adopt a "tough stance" if the government does not clarify its position on the resignation of the Union Education Minister.Speaking to reporters, CJP activist Ashutosh Ranka said his meeting with Union Ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh was constructive, but added that the organisation was still awaiting a response on its primary demand."Yesterday's meeting yielded a positive response regarding compensation and legal matters, reaching an in-principle agreement. We hope to receive that written agreement today. However, no concrete decision has been made regarding our main demand. Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation.""Mainstream media reports suggest sources are saying Pradhan will not step down. If he does not resign, the government should state it clearly, as there is no point in continuing these meetings. We will then decide on our next steps. If the government continues this approach, we will be forced to take a tough stance," Ranka said.Ranka also criticised the Ministry of Education's recent action against 47 National Testing Agency (NTA) officials, saying responsibility ultimately rests with the Education Minister."We will examine the details, but ultimate accountability lies with the Education Minister, who is directly responsible for the paper leaks and the resulting student suicides. He must resign. While we continue to discuss broader reforms and submitted a charter of demands to the government yesterday, his resignation remains key," he added.The CJP has maintained that while discussions with the government on compensation, legal matters and reforms are progressing, its central demand remains the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan.
Article Summary: Cjp founder abhijeet dipke says he has been diagnosed with typhoid. He thanks cjp supporters, whom he referred to as "cockroaches", for carrying out peaceful protests across the country. Cjp activist ashutosh ranka says his meeting with union ministers jp nadda and jitendra singh was constructive.

Article Title: 'Credible threat' from Iran proxies forced Trump to switch planes mid-trip: Report
Article Text: US President Donald Trump switched from a new Qatari-donated Boeing 747-8 to the older Air Force One before departing Turkey earlier this month, according to reports. The move came after US officials identified what they described as a "credible threat" from Iranian proxy forces targeting the president.The New York Times reported earlier that the threat emerged while Trump was attending the Nato summit in Ankara. He had arrived aboard the newly inducted Boeing 747-8, gifted by Qatar, which does not have the same advanced defensive systems as the legacy Air Force One aircraft.Citing people familiar with the matter, the report claimed that after US officials detected the threat, the US secret service recommended that Trump change aircraft before leaving Turkey. The report said the intelligence indicated that Iranian proxy forces were targeting Trump himself rather than the aircraft. However, the newer Boeing's comparatively limited defensive capabilities made flying on it a greater security risk.CBS News confirmed the report later on Friday, saying the US secret service decided to switch planes after receiving intelligence about "a credible plot to fire a missile at the plane".Trump flew to Ankara aboard the new Boeing 747-8, a $400 million Boeing 747-8 that the US accepted as a gift from the Qatari government last year and spent months retrofitting to prepare for it to carry the president. However, after the summit concluded, the US president flew from Ankara to the United Kingdom in the old Air Force One, before switching back to the newer plane to complete his trip back to the United States.The decision prompted fresh questions about the security capabilities of the new aircraft. Citing sources familiar with the matter, the broadcaster reported that the older Air Force One is equipped with laser technology to blind incoming missiles, along with systems designed to misdirect incoming munitions and other defensive countermeasures. It added that it remains unclear what defensive systems are installed on the newer Qatari-donated jet.Earlier this month, Trump did not disclose the security reason behind the aircraft switch, saying he would use the older Air Force One "for old time's sake". He also told reporters that the new aircraft already "has a lot of capability" but would be "maxed out" over the next month as additional upgrades were completed.Trump has repeatedly referred to alleged Iranian threats against his life in recent months. He has previously said he left standing orders for the US military to destroy Iran "at levels they've never seen before" if Tehran carried out what he described as longstanding threats to assassinate him.The latest revelations also come as Trump weighs further military action against Iran following the collapse of a recent ceasefire. Speaking to reporters at the White House on Friday, Trump said, "We are talking to them. I ​think they're being ​serious. I think ... they are ‌being ⁠by far the most serious that we've seen them, but ​that doesn't ​mean ⁠we get there. We'll see ​what happens." He added, "We're locked and loaded. We're ready to go."
Article Summary: Us president donald trump switched from a new qatari-donated boeing 747-8 to the older air force one. The move came after us officials identified what they described as a "credible threat" from iranian proxy forces targeting the president. The decision prompted fresh questions about the security capabilities of the new aircraft.

Article Title: 'Intense, highly unpredictable': Over 200,000 evacuated as massive wildfires engulf Spain, France
Article Text:
Spain, France battle devastating wildfires

More than 200,000 people have either fled or been ordered to remain indoors as massive wildfires swept across Spain and France on Friday.The fires prompted Spain to declare a national emergency, while French authorities ordered the complete evacuation, by land and sea, of one of the country's most popular holiday destinations.Authorities in south-west France ordered the evacuation of the Cap Ferret peninsula on the Atlantic coast "village by village" as an "intense, highly unpredictable" wildfire scorched more than 19,000 hectares (47,000 acres) of forest.In Spain, the government declared its first-ever national emergency over a wildfire after two major blazes merged outside Madrid, while a third fire was close to joining them amid extreme heat and tinder-dry conditions across much of southern Europe.Madrid regional president Isabel Díaz Ayuso described the blaze as the "worst fire in the history of the region", saying the area was facing a "perfect storm" of high temperatures, relentless winds and converging fire fronts.Local emergency services said the wildfires were advancing towards the municipalities of Robledo de Chavela and Fresnedillas de la Oliva, about 50 kilometres (31 miles) from the Spanish capital."The wildfire is at its peak and is currently beyond the capacity of firefighters to contain," Carlos Novillo, the Madrid regional government's emergency management chief, said, as cited by the BBC."It's not possible to attack the fire in that area, so defensive measures are being taken," he added.A national emergency, which allows Spain's central government to assume powers and responsibilities normally held by the country's autonomous regions, has been declared only once before — during the nationwide blackout in April 2025.In south-west France, around 200,000 people have been evacuated as wildfires tore through the Gironde and Landes regions.In the early hours of Saturday, authorities ordered the precautionary evacuation of four towns near Bordeaux: Saint-Médard-en-Jalles, Saint-Jean-d'Illac, Martignas-sur-Jalles and Saint-Aubin-de-Médoc. According to Le Monde, the four municipalities have a combined population of about 58,400.In 2022, a wildfire in south-west France scorched more than 30,000 hectares and forced the evacuation of 50,000 people. Fueled by dry conditions and strong winds, the latest blazes have swept through coastal pine forests, with flames reaching up to 10 metres (30 feet) high.French president Emmanuel Macron said he had activated the European Union's civil protection mechanism as the country battled multiple wildfires after enduring three successive heatwaves since May.Scientists say climate change is making extreme weather events more frequent and more intense by drying out soils and waterways, fuelling wildfires and contributing to thousands of excess deaths. Europe is warming at nearly twice the global average rate.
Article Summary: Spain, france battle devastating wildfires. More than 200,000 people have either fled or been ordered to remain indoors. The fires prompted spain to declare a national emergency over a wildfire. French authorities ordered the complete evacuation of one of the country's most popular holiday destinations.
